\## Summary
Preserve PYTHIA’s substrate-agnostic GPU ontology while making every host execution and release claim explicit and fail closed.

- expose \`hyba-super-gpu\` as the logical substrate when its selected host is \`cpu\`, \`opencl:cpu\`, or \`opencl:gpu\`, while reporting physical GPU availability/count separately;
- allow the exact OpenCL ladder to execute on an identified OpenCL CPU or GPU device and attest the actual \`execution\_backend\`, device name, and vendor;
- accept measured \`opencl:\*\` identities but reject a plain software CPU substitution when a physical OpenCL binding was requested;
- invalidate stale Stratum work on clean-job notifications and keep the listener responsive during grinding;
- distinguish capability detection from active execution, and prevent CPU-reference availability from impersonating a bound production mining device;
- require complete release evidence, create evidence directories, load the canonical behavior policy, and repair canonical dependency/import and container readiness checks.

The operator no-device flow was exercised without connecting to a pool or arming live submission:

!\[Fail-closed operator console\](https://app.devin.ai/api/presigned\_proxy?token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..8ad4PVRNP4ZQhxRJq8f0Y97Asu6Qeoov07Mb8q2vLVc)

The canonical coordinator’s CPU-reference solver is now treated as a valid logical-substrate host, not physical OpenCL evidence. Physical GPU execution, live pool acceptance, and hashrate remain unmeasured.

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/820689c8b8f64bd7beb42e8f04af2cb4
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/820689c8b8f64bd7beb42e8f04af2cb4?variant=devin
